subject: Telemetry & SDK integration checklist for embeddings + routing
message_1_subject: Telemetry & SDK integration checklist for embeddings + routing
message_1_body:
Hi Tanya,

Thanks again for the time today — great to hear more about QuantumPay's fraud-detection pipeline and the places you're looking to add semantic search and reranking. As promised, I put together a concise checklist for the initial integration so your infra and observability teams can review quickly.

Top-level asks: 
- Quick SDK auth decision (API key vs mTLS)
- Routing plan for production vs canary models (policy & headers)
- Embedding storage choices (in-prod vector DB vs transient cache)
- Observability hooks: trace id propagation, per-request latency headers, and structured log fields we recommend

I've attached a spreadsheet with the checklist and a proposed field mapping for logs and trace headers (redwood-telemetry-checklist.xlsx). Can you share who from infra/security should be looped in? Also including Amit on this thread — I think he'll own implementation.

Next steps I propose: 
1) Technical sync with your infra + one of our integration engineers (30–45m) — suggested window Thu or Fri next week.
2) Share infra diagram and any existing SDK constraints (attachments okay).
3) We’ll produce a minimal diffs PR showing header propagation and a sample request/response with the latency breakdown headers.

Thanks — attaching the checklist and the infra template.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
neha@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment(s): redwood-telemetry-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet)
message_2_subject: Re: Telemetry & SDK integration checklist for embeddings + routing
message_2_body:
Neha — thanks, this is very helpful. Looping Amit (lead infra) and me. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

- Auth: security prefers mTLS for production, but we can do API keys for an initial canary. We need your SDK to support both (and clear instructions on cert rotation).
- Routing: we run a feature-proxy that expects an X-Route-Policy header. Can you confirm the SDK can set custom headers per request and the recommended values for canary/model fallback?
- Embeddings: we plan to store vectors in our existing vector store (Pinecone). We’d like recommendations for quantized output and batching settings to avoid cold-start spikes.
- Observability: we require trace‑id propagation across services using traceparent and also want a Redwood-provided X-Redwood-Latency-* header with a per-segment breakdown (ideally: kernel, kv-cache, network, tokenization, generation). Can your runtime emit that?

We can do the technical sync on Friday 2027-04-16 at 10:00 PT — Amit, does that work?

Thanks,
Tanya
Head of Trust & Safety, QuantumPay
tanya@quantumpay.com

message_3_subject: Fwd: Telemetry & SDK integration checklist for embeddings + routing
message_3_body:
Looping in Marissa for observability/solutions input. Quick notes before the sync: 

- SDK auth: we support API keys, OAuth, and mTLS in our private deployments. For a hybrid approach, we'll provide a short 'cert rotation' doc snippet and sample mTLS setup.
- Header support: SDK allows arbitrary request headers. We'll add a small helper to attach X-Route-Policy and X-Env (prod/canary) headers per call.
- Latency headers: runtime can emit X-Redwood-Latency-Total and X-Redwood-Latency-Breakdown. Proposed breakdown keys: kernel, kv_cache, batching_wait_ms, network_ms, tokization_ms, generation_ms. We'll return them as a comma-separated list in the header, and also as structured fields in deidentified logs.
- Trace propagation: we will honor traceparent and also add X-Redwood-Trace-Id for easy correlation with our logs. We recommend you attach both.
- Embedding batching: for Pinecone we recommend micro-batches of 32–128 depending on token length; we'll provide quantization-presets in the checklist.

Action items for the sync (we'll own the demos): 
1) Demo a sample SDK call showing header propagation + trace id.
2) Show a POST body that uses tool-calling/structured output to return a rerank request (we can include a small harness repo).
3) Provide an example log line and a Grafana dashboard URL (we'll share a template you can import).

Attaching internal checklist: redwood-telemetry-checklist.xlsx

—Karthik
Director, Integration Engineering
karthik@redwoodinference.com
message_4_subject: Re: Telemetry & SDK integration checklist for embeddings + routing
message_4_body:
Thanks — Friday 2027-04-16 10:00 PT works for us. A couple of notes to include in the agenda: 

- Please bring a minimal example where the SDK sets X-Route-Policy and shows a fallback to a smaller model if the canary is overloaded. We want to validate the header mapping and the on-the-wire behavior.
- For observability, we need an explicit mapping of Redwood log keys -> our centralized logging schema (we'll share a sample ingestion mapping).
- Can you confirm whether the X-Redwood-Latency-Breakdown header is safe to pass end-user (PII policy)? We prefer that it does not include any raw tokens or user content.

I'll upload our infra diagram to the Drive link you shared and put our logging ingestion mapping there. Look forward to the demo.

—Amit
Engineering Manager, Platform Reliability
Amit Rao <amit@quantumpay.com>
